$schema: Design System Guidelines — Pablo Perea Portfolio
purpose: Authoritative design reference for AI tools generating new pages, case studies, and components. All UI must use the CSS variables and composite text classes defined here — never hardcode colors, spacing, or typography values. The system is responsive by default — typography and spacing tokens scale down on mobile via CSS media queries, and layout components stack vertically on small viewports.

designPhilosophy.summary: A minimal, typographically-driven portfolio that prioritizes content legibility and spatial clarity. Every element earns its place through function, not decoration.

principles.name: Token-first styling
principles.description: All visual properties (color, spacing, radius, typography) must reference CSS custom properties from theme.css. Never hardcode hex colors, pixel values, or font sizes inline. This enables centralized theming and Comfortable/Compact spacing mode switching.

principles.name: Composition over duplication
principles.description: Complex UI is built by composing small, single-purpose DS primitives. For example, ProjectCard with imageVariant='editorial' composes TechnicalSheet + ContentImage + MotionReveal — it owns layout while TechnicalSheet owns the text block. Never duplicate a pattern that already exists as a component.

principles.name: Figma instance-swap parity
principles.description: Components mirror Figma's instance swap architecture: variant props (size, subtitleVariant, ctaType, layout) control which internal sub-component renders, making each component as flexible as its Figma counterpart without code changes.

principles.name: Progressive disclosure of motion
principles.description: Animations are subtle, functional, and scroll-triggered. Content fades in as users scroll — it never jumps or bounces. The MotionReveal primitive standardizes this with 4 animation types. Parallax is reserved for hero images only.

principles.name: Spatial hierarchy through generous whitespace
principles.description: Sections breathe with large padding (72px–96px vertical). Content blocks within sections use moderate gaps (24px–64px). Text elements use tight gaps (4px–16px). This three-tier spacing creates a clear visual hierarchy without decorative dividers.

principles.name: Color restraint
principles.description: The palette is nearly monochrome: dark text on white surfaces, with a single green accent for interactive elements. Color is never used for decoration — it signals actionability (buttons, links, focus rings). Tertiary text and borders create depth through value, not hue.

principles.name: One typeface, two weights
principles.description: Inter at Regular (400) and Medium (500) handles nearly everything from 12px labels to 56px hero headings. Hierarchy is established through size and letter-spacing, not weight proliferation. Weights 600 (SemiBold) and 700 (Bold) are loaded but reserved exclusively for the Navigation brand button — never use them in DS components or page content.

principles.name: Responsive by default via token scaling
principles.description: Responsiveness is achieved through a two-layer hybrid: (1) CSS media queries in theme.css override typography and spacing tokens for mobile viewports — every component automatically adapts with zero code changes, and (2) layout components use Tailwind responsive breakpoints (flex-col md:flex-row) for structural changes like stacking direction. Variables handle global scaling; breakpoints handle layout flow.

fontStack.rule: ONLY use Inter for all generated text. Never introduce additional typefaces.

compositeTextClasses.description: Pre-built CSS classes in index.css that bundle font-size + weight + line-height + letter-spacing from DS tokens. Always use these instead of assembling individual Tailwind utilities.

ds-text-label-eyebrow.usage: Section subtitles, eyebrow text above headings, category labels. Always paired with text-ds-text-tertiary.

ds-text-label-sm.usage: Metadata labels, captions, tooltip text, badge text, tertiary annotations. Usually text-ds-text-tertiary.

ds-text-action-inline.usage: NavButton labels, CaseStudyLink labels, filter pills, breadcrumb text.

ds-text-body-default.usage: Primary paragraph text, descriptions in TechnicalSheet (default/section size), SectionHeader descriptions.

ds-text-body-emphasis.usage: Hero sub-text, TechnicalSheet descriptions in small/large size. Slightly larger body for emphasis contexts.

ds-text-body-compact.usage: Card descriptions, bullet list items, process step descriptions, skill card items. Dense but readable.

ds-text-heading-compact.usage: Card titles, metadata values, process step titles, mobile nav brand text.

ds-text-heading-section.usage: TechnicalSheet title at size='section', stat values in StatItem, About section subheading, QuoteBlock text.

ds-text-heading-overview.usage: TechnicalSheet title at size='small' (used in ProjectOverview). Same font-size as heading-section but different line-height and tracking.

ds-text-heading-page.usage: TechnicalSheet title at default size, ResultCard metrics, process step numbers, QuoteBlock avatar. Primary page-level headings.

ds-text-heading-hero.usage: Hero titles, SectionHeader titles, TechnicalSheet at size='large', case study hero h1. The largest, most impactful text style.

ds-text-data-emphasis.usage: DesignCard metric value at default size.

ds-text-data-default.usage: DesignCard metric value at compact size.

ds-text-data-compact.usage: DesignCard metric heading (small label above the value).

typography.italicUsage: Italic text should be used consciously and purposefully — never as a default pattern across all headings. If a specific heading benefits from editorial emphasis, apply italic to one or two key words via <span className='italic'>. Do not apply italic across every section title in a page.

colors.philosophy: Near-monochrome with one portfolio accent (green). No gradients in UI elements. Color signals function (interactive = green, static = gray scale). Case study pages use a per-project --cs-accent token to brand each project with its own color while keeping the portfolio chrome (nav, CTAs, footer) green.

--ds-text-primary.usage: All headings, card titles, primary labels. The default text color.

--ds-text-secondary.usage: Body paragraphs, descriptions, card subtitles, footer text.

--ds-text-tertiary.usage: Eyebrow labels, captions, metadata labels, muted annotations.

--ds-text-tertiary-inverse.usage: Tertiary text on dark/inverse surfaces. Accessible ~5.4:1 contrast on --ds-surface-inverse. Used by CaseStudyFooter variant='inverse' for the eyebrow label.

--ds-text-inverse.usage: Text on dark backgrounds: primary buttons, dark thumbnails, tooltips, result cards.

--ds-surface-page.usage: Default page background, card content areas, badge backgrounds.

--ds-surface-inverse.usage: Dark backgrounds: solid thumbnails, tooltips, filter pills (selected).

--ds-surface-background.usage: Section backgrounds (Projects, Contact), metric card idle state, case-study-link background.

--ds-action-primary.usage: Primary button background, focus ring color. THE accent green.

--ds-action-subtle.usage: Mobile nav active item background, light green highlight.

--ds-action-hover-primary.usage: Primary button hover, NavButton hover text color.

--ds-action-hover-secondary-inverse.usage: Secondary button hover background on dark/inverse surfaces. Subtle white overlay that keeps --ds-text-inverse readable.

--ds-border-default.usage: Secondary button border, badge border, filter pill border.

--ds-border-subtle.usage: Section dividers, card idle borders, metadata row separators, nav scroll border.

--ds-border-focus.usage: Skill card hover border (green), focus indicator.

--cs-accent.usage: Per-project accent color for case study pages. Set on the page root <div> via inline style. Falls back to portfolio green when unset. Used for: hero backgrounds, numbered pills, exhibit controls (toggles, sliders, checkmarks), annotation highlights, dashed borders.

--cs-accent-text.usage: Text color for content rendered on top of --cs-accent backgrounds (e.g. hero title, numbered pill text). Defaults to dark text. Override per-page if the accent color is dark.

semanticMappings.description: Component-specific CSS variables that alias foundation tokens. This indirection lets you retheme components independently.
examples: Case Study Accent: --cs-accent (page-scoped) — set via inline style on case study root div. Inherited by all children including exhibit components. Falls back to --ds-action-primary (portfolio green) via :root default.

spacing.philosophy: A deliberate 8px-base scale with specific additions (4px, 10px) for micro-adjustments. Spacing modes (Comfortable default, Compact via .spacing-compact class) scale all values proportionally.

--ds-space-4.usage: Tightest gap: subtitle-to-title in TechnicalSheet, NavButton internal gaps.

--ds-space-8.usage: Badge gaps in tag rows, text block internal gaps, skill card item spacing.

--ds-space-10.usage: Button icon-to-text gap, bullet dot vertical offset.

--ds-space-12.usage: Filter pill padding, tooltip padding, bullet list item spacing, badge label-to-list gap.

--ds-space-16.usage: Button padding (default), SectionHeader internal gap, result card metric-to-description, process step title-to-description.

--ds-space-24.usage: Page horizontal padding (mobile), TechnicalSheet outer gap, card internal padding, grid gaps, hero label-to-title.

--ds-space-32.usage: Button padding (default horizontal), Hero content gaps, metadata section gaps, social card row gaps.

--ds-space-48.usage: Section internal gaps (hero, cta, contact), horizontal card layout gap, page padding (desktop), button padding (large horizontal).

--ds-space-64.usage: ProjectCard (editorial/scrollReveal) grid gap, ProjectOverview grid gap, process grid header-to-grid spacing, hero bottom padding.

--ds-space-72.usage: Section vertical padding, About section top, DesignSection projects/cta gap.

--ds-space-96.usage: Large section vertical padding (desktop), ProjectCard spaced bottom margin, hero bottom padding (desktop).

--ds-space-102.usage: Largest gap: between project cards in the home ProjectsSection stack.

spacing.tailwindUsage: Use Tailwind's DS spacing utilities: px-ds-24, gap-ds-48, py-ds-72, mb-ds-96, etc. The @theme inline block maps --spacing-ds-XX for each token.

responsiveness.strategy: Two-layer hybrid: CSS token overrides for global scaling (typography + spacing), Tailwind breakpoints for structural layout changes (stacking direction). This means ~80% of responsive adaptation happens automatically through variables, with only layout-flow changes requiring component-level breakpoints.
responsiveness.breakpoint: 767px (max-width) — aligns with Tailwind's md: breakpoint at 768px.

layer1_tokenOverrides.placement: After :root, BEFORE .spacing-compact (so compact mode wins via later source order at equal specificity).

typography.description: Scales down large heading and data font sizes for mobile readability. Small text (labels, body-compact, actions) is untouched — already mobile-appropriate.

lineHeights.description: Scaled proportionally to match reduced font sizes.

tracking.description: Loosens tight negative tracking at smaller sizes — tight tracking designed for 48-56px doesn't work at 28-36px.

spacing.description: Compresses large gaps for smaller viewports. Small spacing (4-32px) is untouched.

componentsAffected: TechnicalSheet — all size variants auto-scale (heading-hero/page/section/overview + body text)
SectionHeader — heading-hero title + body-default description auto-scale

layer2_layoutBreakpoints.description: Structural layout changes that cannot be expressed with CSS variables. These require Tailwind responsive classes in component code.

ProjectCard.change: Horizontal layouts (left/right) stack vertically on mobile
ProjectCard.mobile: flex-col gap-ds-24 — thumbnail on top, text below (natural reading order)
ProjectCard.rightVariant: Uses md:order-first on the sheet block wrapper to swap text before thumbnail on desktop, while keeping thumbnail-first DOM order for mobile stacking

otherResponsiveComponents: Hero — typographic layout, single column (flex-col), no breakpoint-driven layout swap needed
ProjectCard (editorial/mockup) — flex-col md:flex-row, stacks on mobile (already responsive)
ProjectOverview — lg:grid-cols-[2fr_1fr], stacks on mobile (already responsive)
AllProjects grid — md:grid-cols-2, single-col on mobile (already responsive)
About card grid — grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2, cards stack on phones (<640px)
Navigation — desktop NavButtons hidden on mobile, MobileNav drawer shown instead (already responsive)

spacingCompactInteraction.description: If .spacing-compact class is applied alongside the mobile media query, compact mode wins (later source order, equal specificity). This is intentional — explicit compact mode is a stronger override than viewport-based compression.

steps: 3. If spacing, also add compact value in .spacing-compact {}
4. Map to Tailwind in @theme inline {} if it needs a utility class

--ds-radius-sm.usage: NavButton, DesignThumbnail, mobile nav items, tooltips.

--ds-border-width-default.usage: Standard border on badges, cards, filters, buttons.

borders.tailwindUsage: Use rounded-ds-sm, rounded-ds-md, rounded-ds-lg, rounded-ds-xl, rounded-ds-pill. For widths: border-ds-default, border-ds-focus.

--ds-max-w-content.usage: Site-wide content column max-width for all homepage sections (Hero, ProjectsSection, About, Contact). Defined in theme.css :root. Changing it once resizes every section simultaneously.

--ds-aspect-hero-image.usage: Portrait aspect ratio of the Hero thumbnail. Applied via style={{ aspectRatio: 'var(--ds-aspect-hero-image)' }} on the image wrapper in Hero.tsx.

maxWidths.--ds-max-w-content (1386px): Token-based site-wide content column. Used as max-w-(--ds-max-w-content) on the inner content wrapper of every homepage section (Hero, ProjectsSection, About, Contact). Changing the token in theme.css resizes all sections at once.
maxWidths.max-w-7xl (1280px): Case study pages, AllProjects grid, CaseStudySection inner container, page footers.
maxWidths.max-w-4xl: Constrained width for standalone TechnicalSheet blocks (challenge sections, solution headers).
maxWidths.max-w-[672px]: Centered description text cap in TechnicalSheet to maintain comfortable line length.

gridPatterns.projectCards_home: Single column stack with gap-ds-102 (largest spacing). Alternating left/right layout prop on ProjectCard.
gridPatterns.projectCards_allProjects: 2-column grid (md:grid-cols-2) with gap-x-ds-32, gap-y-ds-48. All cards use layout='top' with sheetSize='small'.
gridPatterns.solutionBlocks: 2-column grid (lg:grid-cols-2) with gap-ds-64. Image/text sides alternate via imagePosition prop.
gridPatterns.challengeCards: 3-column grid (md:grid-cols-3) with gap-ds-32. Metric cards with compact size.
gridPatterns.processSteps: 4-column grid (lg:grid-cols-4) with gap-px + bg-border (creates 1px dividers). Rounded-ds-xl container.
gridPatterns.aboutGrid: Responsive grid (grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2) with gap-ds-24. Cards stack on phones (<640px), go side-by-side on sm+. Metric and skill cards have padding+borders that need full-width on small phones.
gridPatterns.statItemGrid: 2-column grid (grid-cols-2) with gap-ds-24 inside case study research sections. Kept always 2-col because StatItem content is inherently compact (short numbers + wrapping labels). Unlike DesignCards, no padding/border makes 2-col safe even at 320px.
gridPatterns.metadata: 2:1 grid (lg:grid-cols-[2fr_1fr]) with gap-ds-64 lg:gap-ds-96 for ProjectOverview.

responsiveBreakpoints.mobile: < 768px (md). Single column layouts, reduced horizontal padding (px-ds-24).
responsiveBreakpoints.tablet: 768px+ (md). Two-column grids activate, navigation shows desktop items.
responsiveBreakpoints.desktop: 1024px+ (lg). Full multi-column layouts, extended horizontal padding (px-ds-48).

sectionPadding.horizontal: px-ds-24 (mobile) → lg:px-ds-48 (desktop). Applied to the Layer 2 inner content-wrapper <div> (NOT on the <section> tag itself, and NOT via DesignSection className). The three-layer pattern is: <section id background> → <div max-w-(--ds-max-w-content) mx-auto px-ds-24 lg:px-ds-48> → <DesignSection variant>. CaseStudySection handles its own padding internally.
sectionPadding.vertical: Handled by DesignSection variant classes (py-ds-48 for projects, py-ds-72 for cta/hero, py-ds-96 for About). Never apply py-* to the outer <section> tag except when not using DesignSection (e.g. About which applies py-ds-96 directly on the section).

animation.library: Motion (motion/react) — formerly Framer Motion. Import as: import { motion } from 'motion/react'

primitive.description: Universal animation wrapper. Use this instead of raw motion.div.

slide-up.usage: Default for most content blocks, text sections, cards.

scale.usage: Images, cards that should feel like they 'pop' into view.

fade.usage: Subtle reveals for footer text, secondary content.

triggerModes.inView: Default. Fires when element enters viewport (margin: -100px). Once: true.
triggerModes.mount: Fires immediately on component mount. Used for above-fold content on route change (AllProjects grid, hero content).

primitive.staggerPattern: For lists/grids, wrap each item in MotionReveal with delay={index * 0.1} (cards) or delay={index * 0.06} (dense grids). Keep duration at 0.5-0.6s for staggered items.

parallax.effect: Background image translates 0→30% on scroll. Opacity fades 1→0 at 80% scroll.
parallax.usage: ONLY for case study hero sections. Never parallax regular page content.

microInteractions.navigation: initial: y -100, animate: y 0, duration 0.6s (slides down on page load)
microInteractions.arrows: Scroll indicator arrow bounces (y: [0, 8, 0]) on hover with 1.5s infinite repeat

behavior.type: Single adaptive bar — adapts right-side content based on route.

brandButton.note: The brand button is the ONLY element in the project that uses font-weight 600 (SemiBold). This is an intentional design choice — do not replicate this weight elsewhere.

homeMode.right_desktop: Section NavButtons with scroll-spy (Home, Proyectos, Sobre mi, Contacto) + animated underline (layoutId='activeSection')

subpageMode.right_desktop: Inline breadcrumb: NavButton(icon) 'Portfolio' > Chevron > [optional: 'Todos los proyectos' >] 'Case Study Title'. Reads ?from=allProjects search param.
subpageMode.right_mobile: Compact NavButton(icon) back button to last clickable parent breadcrumb.

navigation.addingCaseStudy: Add slug → title mapping to CASE_STUDY_TITLES record in Navigation.tsx.

components.overview: ~30 reusable Figma-mapped components in /src/app/components/ds/, barrel-exported from index.ts (~33 named exports). Import: import { ComponentName } from '../../components/ds';

primitives.description: Atomic building blocks — no internal composition with other DS components.

DesignButton.purpose: Primary and secondary action buttons with optional icon — supports directional arrows or any DesignIcon.

variants.primary: Green fill (--btn-primary-bg), white text, hover darkens + shadow.
variants.secondary: Transparent with border overlay (--btn-secondary-border), hover adds green-tint bg + shadow.

iconProps.icon: boolean — whether to show an icon.
iconProps.iconType: 'arrow' (default) renders DesignArrow; any DesignIconName (e.g. 'mail', 'github', 'linkedin') renders the corresponding DesignIcon. Fully backward-compatible — omitting iconType gives arrow behavior.
iconProps.iconDirection: Arrow pointing direction (8 values). Only used when iconType='arrow'. Default: 'right'.
iconProps.iconPosition: 'left' | 'right' — which side of the text the icon renders. Default: 'left'. INDEPENDENT from iconDirection and iconType.

NavButton.purpose: Navigation link with state-based color and optional back-arrow icon + underline.

states.selected: opacity-100, color --nav-btn-text (#141411), optional animated underline bar

props.icon: Shows left-pointing back arrow (only when NOT selected).
props.underline: Shows/hides the animated underline when selected. Default true.
props.layoutId: Shared layout ID for the underline animation across a group of NavButtons.

DesignArrow.purpose: Directional arrow icon with 8 directions, each using a dedicated SVG path (no CSS rotation).

Chevron.purpose: Small directional chevron for breadcrumbs and navigation separators.

DesignIcon.purpose: Figma-exported SVG icons for domain-specific use cases.

DesignBadge.purpose: Pill-shaped tag for skills, tools, and categories.
DesignBadge.styling: rounded-ds-lg, border --badge-border, bg --badge-bg, ds-text-label-sm, px-ds-16 py-ds-8

variants.filled: Dark bg (--primary), white text. Used in hero overlays.
variants.subtle: Transparent bg, tertiary text. For secondary labels.

DesignFilter.purpose: Category filter pill with idle/hover/selected states.

variants.solid: Dark bg (--dthumb-bg), white icon. Always-on dark state for skill cards.
variants.interactive: White idle → dark on parent hover. Icon color inverts. Needs parent group/card.

StatItem.purpose: Large metric + small label. Used in research sections of case studies.

BulletList.purpose: Vertical list with 1.5px dot bullets. Used inside ProjectCard/TechnicalSheet children slot.
BulletList.styling: space-y-ds-12, ds-text-body-compact text-ds-text-secondary, bullet dot bg-ds-text-primary

ContentImage.purpose: Responsive image with rounded container, configurable aspect ratio, and optional caption.
ContentImage.caption: ds-text-label-sm text-ds-text-tertiary mt-ds-16 text-center

DSTooltip.styling: bg-ds-surface-inverse text-ds-text-inverse, px-ds-12 py-ds-8, rounded-ds-sm, max-w-[240px], ds-text-label-sm

StepList.purpose: Numbered vertical stepper for syncing annotated step copy with IPhoneMockup frames. Designed to sit in the children slot of TechnicalSheet (via ProjectCard). Bidirectional: clicking a step pill or row fires onStepChange (which advances the mockup); the mockup advancing (onMockupFrameChange) updates the same parent state, which in turn sets activeStep.

visualAnatomy.leftColumn: 32px numbered pill (ds-space-32 circle) + flex-grow vertical connector line (border-subtle, 1px wide) that stretches to match each row's content height.
visualAnatomy.rightColumn: Step title (always visible) + description (visible only on active step, animated height open/close via motion/react AnimatePresence).

states.active: Pill filled ds-action-primary, text ds-text-inverse. Title ds-text-primary + ds-font-weight-medium. Description expanded.
states.inactive: Pill transparent, border ds-border-default, text ds-text-tertiary. Title ds-text-secondary + ds-font-weight-regular. Description hidden.
states.hoverInactive: Pill border and title color shift to ds-text-primary (via local hoveredIndex state). Cursor pointer.

StepList.typography: All text uses ds-font-size-body-compact, ds-line-height-body-compact, ds-tracking-body-compact, ds-font-family. Pill number uses ds-font-size-label-lg.

props.steps: StepItem[] — { title: string; description?: string }[]. Length MUST equal mockupFrames.length on the sibling ProjectCard.
props.activeStep: number — controlled, owned by parent page. Never manage this inside StepList.
props.onStepChange: (index: number) => void — update the same state that drives activeMockupFrame on ProjectCard.
props.className: optional string on the outer wrapper.

StepList.stateOwnership: ALWAYS in the parent page component. StepList is fully controlled. The same state drives both activeMockupFrame (on ProjectCard) and activeStep (on StepList).
StepList.rule: steps.length must equal mockupFrames.length — one step per frame. Mismatching lengths produces out-of-sync UI.
StepList.animation: AnimatePresence + motion.div with height: 0→auto, opacity: 0→1, duration 0.25s easeInOut. overflow: hidden on the motion wrapper prevents clipping during transition.
StepList.usagePattern: const [activeStep, setActiveStep] = useState(0); → pass activeMockupFrame={activeStep} onMockupFrameChange={setActiveStep} to ProjectCard and activeStep={activeStep} onStepChange={setActiveStep} to StepList inside the children slot.

compositions.description: Higher-order components that compose primitives into reusable patterns.

TechnicalSheet.role: UNIVERSAL TEXT BLOCK PRIMITIVE. The single most important composition component.
TechnicalSheet.structure: Vertical stack (gap-ds-24): [TextBlock(gap-ds-8: SubtitleTitle(gap-ds-4) + Description)] → [Children slot] → [Tags row] → [CTA slot]

align.centered: items-center text-center, description capped at max-w-[672px]

TechnicalSheet.childrenSlot: Flexible ReactNode below description. Accepts BulletList, stat grids, custom badge layouts, or any content.
TechnicalSheet.usageGuideline: When you need a subtitle + title + description + optional content + optional badges + optional CTA, ALWAYS use TechnicalSheet. Do not recreate this pattern manually.

SectionHeader.role: Simplified heading block for page-level section titles. Intentionally kept separate from TechnicalSheet.
SectionHeader.structure: Vertical stack (gap-ds-4): subtitle (label-eyebrow/tertiary, leading-none) → title (heading-hero/primary, leading-none) → description (body-default/secondary). Both subtitle and title use leading-none so the CSS gap maps directly to visible glyph-to-glyph spacing.
SectionHeader.whenToUse: Use for the top-level heading of Home page sections (Proyectos, Sobre mi) and AllProjects page header. For everything else, use TechnicalSheet.

DesignSection.role: Layout container with Figma-mapped section variants.

variants.hero: flex gap-ds-48 items-center py-ds-72 overflow-clip (NOTE: the current Hero.tsx does NOT use DesignSection — it has its own layout. This variant is preserved for potential future use or alternative hero layouts)
variants.pageFooter: flex-col md:flex-row justify-between items-center gap-ds-24 pt-ds-48 border-t border-ds-border-subtle

CaseStudySection.role: Standard section wrapper for case study pages. Handles padding + max-width + optional accent bg.
CaseStudySection.styling: py-ds-72 md:py-ds-96 px-ds-24 lg:px-ds-48, inner max-w-7xl mx-auto
CaseStudySection.accentProp: accent={true} adds bg-accent/30 for alternating visual rhythm.

ProjectCard.role: UNIFIED project showcase card. Replaced both the old ProjectCard and the deleted SolutionBlock. Composes ProjectThumbnail | ContentImage | IPhoneMockup (selected via imageVariant) with TechnicalSheet.

layouts.left: Horizontal: image left, sheet right. Desktop: flex-row gap-ds-48. Mobile: stacks vertically (flex-col gap-ds-24, image on top). Default showCta: true.
layouts.right: Horizontal: sheet left, image right. Desktop: flex-row gap-ds-48 with md:order-first on sheet. Mobile: stacks vertically (image on top). Default showCta: true.
layouts.top: Vertical: image top, sheet below. gap-ds-24. Default showCta: false. Always vertical at all breakpoints.

imageVariants.thumbnail: ProjectThumbnail — hover-zoom + gradient overlay. For portfolio listing cards. Props: image, alt, zoom, imageClassName.
imageVariants.editorial: ContentImage — plain rounded image, no hover. For case study solution sections. Props: image, alt, imageAspectRatio, imageRounded, imageCaption.
imageVariants.mockup: IPhoneMockup — iPhone 16 SVG frame with navigable frames. For app screen walkthroughs. Props: mockupFrames, mockupMaxWidth, activeMockupFrame, onMockupFrameChange.

mockupProps.mockupFrames: (string | ReactNode)[] — required when imageVariant='mockup'. Accepts screenshot URL strings or React elements (e.g. interactive prototype screens). One item per frame/step.
mockupProps.mockupMaxWidth: CSS max-width of the mockup container. Default '280px'.
mockupProps.activeMockupFrame: number — controlled frame index, driven by parent state.
mockupProps.onMockupFrameChange: (i: number) => void — fires when user clicks left/right half of the phone or dot indicators.

ProjectCard.childrenSlot: ReactNode forwarded to TechnicalSheet's children slot. Accepts BulletList, StatItem grids, StepList, or any content. When using StepList here, set showCta={false} — the steps serve as the navigation CTA.
ProjectCard.sheetProps: subtitle, subtitleVariant ('eyebrow'|'label'), title, description, sheetAlign, sheetSize forwarded verbatim to TechnicalSheet.

behaviorProps.scrollReveal: Wraps each column in its own MotionReveal for independent scroll entrance.
behaviorProps.spaced: Adds mb-ds-96 below the card — use on all solution blocks except the last.

ProjectCard.responsiveBehavior: Horizontal layouts use flex-col md:flex-row with gap-ds-24 md:gap-ds-48. The right variant uses md:order-first on the sheet wrapper to swap order on desktop while keeping image-first for mobile stacking. Layer 2 layout breakpoint — typography and spacing handled by Layer 1 token overrides.

patterns.portfolioListingCard: layout='left|right', imageVariant='thumbnail' (default), image, alt (dedicated string — not project.title), tags, subtitle, title, description, ctaLabel, onCtaClick, zoom (from data), showCta (from data). All per-project values live in the ProjectData array — never compute inline.
patterns.caseStudySolutionBlock: layout='left|right', imageVariant='editorial', subtitleVariant='label', sheetSize='section', scrollReveal, spaced (omit on last). Optional children: BulletList.
patterns.iPhoneMockupCard: layout='right', imageVariant='mockup', mockupFrames=[...], activeMockupFrame={step}, onMockupFrameChange={setStep}, showCta={false}. Children: StepList with matching steps array and same state.

ProjectCard.homeUsage: layout='left'|'right' alternating, imageVariant='thumbnail', default sheetSize, with CTA links.
ProjectCard.allProjectsUsage: layout='top', imageVariant='thumbnail', sheetSize='small', no CTA, wrapped in clickable div.

ProjectThumbnail.role: Image container with hover gradient overlay and subtle scale animation.
ProjectThumbnail.features: group/thumbnail scoping, zoom prop (wrapper scale), 1.02 scale on hover, gradient fadeIn on hover.

ProjectOverview.role: Case study overview section: TechnicalSheet (2fr) + ProjectMetadata (1fr) in responsive grid.
ProjectOverview.structure: grid lg:grid-cols-[2fr_1fr] gap-ds-64 lg:gap-ds-96. Both columns have slide-up entrance.

ProjectMetadata.role: Vertical metadata list with border-separated label/value rows + optional tag badges.
ProjectMetadata.structure: flex-col gap-ds-32. Each row: label (ds-text-label-sm/tertiary) + value (ds-text-heading-compact/primary) + border-b.

SolutionBlock.role: DEPRECATED. Consolidated into ProjectCard with imageVariant='editorial'. Do not recreate this file.
SolutionBlock.migration: Replace any SolutionBlock usage with ProjectCard: <ProjectCard imageVariant='editorial' subtitleVariant='label' sheetSize='section' scrollReveal spaced layout='left|right' image={...} title={...} description={...}><BulletList items={[...]} /></ProjectCard>
SolutionBlock.note: The SolutionBlock component no longer exists in the codebase. All its functionality is covered by ProjectCard.

ProcessGrid.role: 4-step numbered process section with optional wireframe image.
ProcessGrid.composition: TechnicalSheet (header) → grid of ProcessStep in MotionReveal → optional ContentImage
ProcessGrid.gridStyle: gap-px bg-border rounded-ds-xl overflow-hidden (creates 1px divider lines between steps).

ProcessStep.role: Individual step card: faded number + title + description.
ProcessStep.styling: bg-background p-ds-32 lg:p-ds-48. Number: ds-text-heading-page text-ds-text-secondary/30.

ResultGrid.role: Dark metric cards grid with centered header. Also accepts mockupFrames to replace the metric-card grid with a centred IPhoneMockup.
ResultGrid.composition: TechnicalSheet (align='centered', header) → grid of ResultCard in MotionReveal (default), or centred IPhoneMockup when mockupFrames provided.
ResultGrid.resultCard: bg-primary text-primary-foreground rounded-ds-md p-ds-32. Metric: ds-text-heading-page. Description: ds-text-label-sm opacity-70.
ResultGrid.mockupMode: Pass mockupFrames prop to render a centred IPhoneMockup instead of ResultCard grid. Used for 'Prueba el prototipo completo' sections.

QuoteBlock.role: Centered testimonial/reflection quote with avatar circle.
QuoteBlock.structure: text-center space-y-ds-32: avatar circle (64px, bg-primary) → blockquote (ds-text-heading-section) → author (ds-text-heading-compact) + subtitle (ds-text-label-sm/tertiary)

CaseStudyFooter.role: Bottom CTA section for case studies. Thank-you message + back/contact buttons. Supports variant='inverse' for dark background with accessible text.
CaseStudyFooter.composition: TechnicalSheet (size='section', subtitleVariant='label') + two DesignButtons (secondary back + primary contact)
CaseStudyFooter.layout: flex-col md:flex-row justify-between items-center, py-ds-72 md:py-ds-96

variants.default: border-t border-ds-border-subtle, inherits page background. Standard text colors.
variants.inverse: bg-ds-surface-inverse, no top border. Scoped CSS variable overrides on the <section> style attribute remap --ds-text-primary → --ds-text-inverse, --ds-text-secondary → --ds-text-inverse, --ds-text-tertiary → --ds-text-tertiary-inverse (#A89F9F), --btn-secondary-text/border → --ds-text-inverse, --icon-foreground → --ds-text-inverse. All composed children (TechnicalSheet, DesignButton) inherit the inverse palette automatically — no per-child overrides needed.

props.label: Eyebrow text. Default: 'Gracias por leer'. Renders as tertiary text (--ds-text-tertiary on default, --ds-text-tertiary-inverse on inverse).
props.heading: Heading text. Default: '¿Interesado en trabajar juntos?'.
props.backLabel: Back button label. Default: 'Volver a Home'.

CaseStudyFooter.accessibilityNote: The inverse variant uses --ds-text-tertiary-inverse (#A89F9F) for the eyebrow label, providing ~5.4:1 contrast ratio on --ds-surface-inverse (#292925). This passes WCAG AA for normal text.

ParallaxHero.role: Full-viewport hero with parallax background image and gradient overlay.
ParallaxHero.structure: Full viewport height (85vh mobile, 90vh desktop). Parallax image (0→30% translateY). Gradient: from-background via-background/40 to-transparent. Bottom-aligned children with entrance animation.
ParallaxHero.usage: ONLY for case study page tops. Never use for Home hero or regular sections.

DesignCard.role: Multi-variant card for stats, skills, social links, and numbered principles.

variants.metric: Large stat value + description. Hover: bg darkens, border thickens. Used in About stats and case study challenges.
variants.skill: Dark thumbnail + title + item list. Hover: green border + shadow. Used in About skills.
variants.social: Thumbnail + title/subtitle + hover arrow. Used in Contact section.
variants.numbered: Accent-filled number pill (--cs-accent bg, --cs-accent-text color, 32px circle) + title + description. No hover effects. Used for design constraints/principles in case studies. The pill inherits the per-project accent color automatically.

numberedProps.number: string — formatted number for the pill (e.g. '01')
numberedProps.title: string — card title

responsiveBehavior.strategy: Differentiated scaling per variant — NOT uniform downscale. The DesignCard component itself has no breakpoints; responsiveness comes from Layer 1 token scaling and parent grid layout.
responsiveBehavior.metric_default: ds-text-data-emphasis (36→28px) auto-scales via Layer 1. Card padding (p-ds-32) stays fixed. Parent About grid stacks to 1-col on phones (<640px).
responsiveBehavior.metric_compact: ds-text-data-default (24→20px) auto-scales via Layer 1. Used in case study challenge grids (md:grid-cols-3 → 1-col). Moderate reduction.
responsiveBehavior.skill: Uses ds-text-heading-compact (16px) + ds-text-body-compact (14px) — both untouched by mobile overrides. Already mobile-appropriate. No font scaling needed.
responsiveBehavior.social: Same small text classes as skill. No font scaling needed. Parent Contact layout already stacks (flex-col md:flex-row).
responsiveBehavior.numbered: Uses ds-text-heading-compact (16px) + ds-text-body-compact (14px) — same as skill, already mobile-appropriate. Parent grid handles stacking (md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 → 1-col on mobile).

IPhoneMockup.role: Standalone iPhone 16 Natural Titanium SVG mockup for showcasing app screens. Used internally by ProjectCard when imageVariant='mockup'. Scalable vector, viewBox 0 0 390 804.

modes.static: Single item in frames array → renders a fixed screenshot inside the phone frame.
modes.navigable: Multiple frames → dot-navigable carousel. Click left half to retreat, right half to advance.
modes.controlled: Provide activeFrame + onFrameChange to drive from parent state — required for StepList bidirectional sync.
modes.uncontrolled: Omit activeFrame + onFrameChange — manages its own internal index. Zero-prop standalone usage.

props.frames: (string | ReactNode)[] — screenshot image URLs or React elements. Required.
props.onFrameChange: (i: number) => void — fires on left/right click or dot tap (optional).
props.scrollHint: boolean — shows a persistent 'Try scrolling' chip with a Mouse icon below the phone frame, with a slow bobbing animation. Use for scrollable ReactNode frames to signal interactivity. Renders in the portfolio canvas layer, never overlaid on the app screen.
props.interactiveHint: boolean — enables Figma-style interactive hotspot discovery. On first scroll-into-view, all [data-hotspot] elements inside the screen flash with a blue pulse (one-time entrance hint). When the user clicks the screen but misses a [data-hotspot] element, the hotspots flash again. Prototype screens must mark their interactive elements with the data-hotspot HTML attribute.

IPhoneMockup.dotStyling: Active dot: ds-action-primary fill. Inactive dot: ds-border-default stroke, transparent fill.
IPhoneMockup.usageNote: Prefer via ProjectCard (imageVariant='mockup') for layout composition. Use standalone only when the mockup is needed outside a ProjectCard context.

variants.default: Plain text + arrow. Hover: translates 4px right.

MobileNav.role: Sheet drawer for mobile navigation. Wraps shadcn Sheet with DS styling.
MobileNav.structure: Brand header (border-b) → nav items (rounded-ds-sm buttons) → footer (email link, border-t)

BreadcrumbNav.role: Reusable pill-shaped breadcrumb. Currently unused (Navigation.tsx handles breadcrumbs inline). Kept as a DS primitive for potential future use.

MotionReveal.role: Universal scroll-reveal animation wrapper. Use this instead of raw motion.div for all content entrance animations.
MotionReveal.rule: Every content block that enters the viewport should be wrapped in MotionReveal. Only use raw motion.div for micro-interactions (hover, press, layout animations).

structure: Hero — Full viewport, typographic hero (no image). Single heading-hero h1 statement (with green accent on name) + two DesignButtons (primary 'Ver Proyectos' + secondary 'Contáctame') + scroll indicator arrow at bottom. No eyebrow text.
ProjectsSection — bg-ds-surface-background, SectionHeader + alternating ProjectCards (left/right) with gap-ds-102 + 'Ver Todos' button
About — SectionHeader + bio text (left, body-default/secondary) + 2×2 card grid (right: 2 metric + 2 skill DesignCards)
Contact — bg-ds-surface-background, centered TechnicalSheet + large DesignButton (mail icon) + 3 social DesignCards + footer
home.scrollSections: Each section has an id (home, projects, about, contact) for scroll-spy navigation.
home.heroNote: The Hero section uses a pure typographic approach — no hero image. The --ds-aspect-hero-image token is preserved in theme.css for potential future use but is NOT currently rendered. The Hero does NOT use DesignSection; it uses its own flex layout (flex-col gap-ds-48 py-ds-72).

structure: Top padding: pt-32 md:pt-40 (clears 80px nav + breathing room)
SectionHeader (subtitle + title + description)
DesignFilter row for category filtering
2-column grid of ProjectCard layout='top' sheetSize='small'
Page footer (DesignSection variant='pageFooter') with count + back button
allProjects.filterBehavior: Derive categories from project data with 'All' prepended. Active filter highlights with dark bg.

CaseStudySection — ProjectOverview (description + metadata sidebar)
[optional] Full-width ContentImage break (outside CaseStudySection, with MotionReveal)
CaseStudySection — Challenge (TechnicalSheet + DesignCard metric/compact grid, or custom stats)
CaseStudySection — Research (TechnicalSheet + StatItem grid + ContentImage, in lg:grid-cols-2)
[variant A] CaseStudySection — ProcessGrid (4 numbered steps + optional wireframe)
[variant B] CaseStudySection — UserFlowDiagram (for flow-centric case studies like Invest)
CaseStudySection — Solution header (TechnicalSheet in max-w-4xl) + 3× ProjectCard (editorial or mockup, scrollReveal, spaced except last)
CaseStudySection — ResultGrid (centered header + 4 dark metric cards, OR mockupFrames with interactive prototype)
[optional] CaseStudySection — QuoteBlock (centered reflection quote)
[optional] CaseStudySection — 'Aprendizajes clave' learnings grid (TechnicalSheet header + md:grid-cols-3 of h3 ds-text-heading-compact + p ds-text-body-default/secondary, each in MotionReveal)
CaseStudyFooter variant='inverse' — dark background thank-you CTA with back + contact buttons
caseStudy.accentAlternation: Alternate accent={true/false} on CaseStudySections for visual rhythm. The exact pattern varies per case study — there is no single fixed sequence. The general principle: adjacent sections should alternate where possible, but content needs (e.g. full-width image breaks, learnings grids) may require consecutive non-accent sections. Current patterns: Invest (normal→accent→normal→accent→normal→accent→footer), Audio (normal→normal→normal→accent→normal→accent→normal→accent→normal→footer), Shipping (normal→accent→normal→accent→normal→normal→accent→footer).

learningsSection.description: Optional 'Aprendizajes clave' section used in Audio and Shipping case studies. Not a DS component — built inline with existing primitives.
learningsSection.pattern: CaseStudySection > MotionReveal(TechnicalSheet subtitle='Reflexión' title='Aprendizajes clave') + grid md:grid-cols-3 gap-ds-32 > MotionReveal(h3 ds-text-heading-compact + p ds-text-body-default text-ds-text-secondary) per learning item. Each item gets staggered delay (index * 0.15, duration 0.6).

uniqueFeatures: Interactive prototype screens (AssetInfoScreen, InvestmentSetupScreen, RiskClarificationScreen) as ReactNode mockupFrames
ResultGrid with iframe-based Figma prototype + 'Reiniciar prototipo' button
Solution blocks all use layout='left' with imageVariant='mockup'
Full-width ContentImage break between Overview and Challenge
Solution blocks all use layout='left' with imageVariant='mockup' (static images)
Problem section uses raw stat divs (ds-text-heading-section text-ds-action-primary) instead of StatItem component
Solution blocks alternate layout='left'/'right'/'left' with imageVariant='editorial'
Standard ResultGrid with metric cards (no mockup)

steps: 1. Create /src/app/pages/case-study/CaseStudy[Name].tsx following the section structure above.
2. Add a case to the switch in CaseStudyPage.tsx mapping slug → component.
3. Add slug → title to CASE_STUDY_TITLES in Navigation.tsx for breadcrumb support. CRITICAL: forgetting this step means breadcrumbs show the raw slug instead of a readable title.
4. Add project entry to the projects arrays in ProjectsSection.tsx and AllProjects.tsx with hasCaseStudy: true and the slug.

5. All section content should use DS components (TechnicalSheet, ProjectCard with appropriate imageVariant, ResultGrid, ProcessGrid, QuoteBlock, ContentImage, BulletList, StatItem, DesignLabel, DesignCard). Solution blocks use ProjectCard with imageVariant='editorial' or 'mockup'. SolutionBlock is deprecated.
6. Wrap content blocks in MotionReveal for scroll-reveal. Use CaseStudySection for consistent padding/max-width.
7. Use unsplash images (never hallucinate URLs). Set useEffect scrollTo(0,0) at mount.

notFound.structure: Centered TechnicalSheet (align='centered') with DesignButton back to home. Min-height 80vh.

routing.rootLayout: RootLayout wraps all pages with Navigation + AnimatePresence (mode='wait') for crossfade transitions.
routing.frozenOutlet: FrozenOutlet pattern freezes the outlet ref so exit animations render the old page, not the new one. IMPORTANT: useLocation() inside frozen components returns stale location.state — use URL search params (?from=allProjects) instead.

routes.description: Dynamic case study. Switch statement maps slug to component.

fileStructure./src/styles/fonts.css: Google Fonts import for Inter 400+500+600+700. Font faces defined here ONLY. Weights 600/700 reserved for Navigation brand button.
fileStructure./src/styles/tailwind.css: Tailwind v4 base import (@import 'tailwindcss' source(none)) + source directive + tw-animate-css.
fileStructure./src/styles/theme.css: FIVE top-level blocks (NEVER nest): :root (all foundation tokens + semantic vars), @media max-width:767px (responsive mobile overrides), .spacing-compact (explicit compact spacing), .dark (dark mode overrides), @theme inline (Tailwind v4 mappings). CRITICAL: @theme inline MUST be a top-level directive, not nested inside :root. The @media block must come AFTER :root but BEFORE .spacing-compact so compact mode wins via source order.
fileStructure./src/styles/index.css: Import chain (fonts → tailwind → theme) + html base styles + composite text class definitions (.ds-text-*).

tokenNamingConvention.tailwindMapping: @theme inline maps foundation tokens for Tailwind utility generation: --color-ds-text-primary, --spacing-ds-24, --radius-ds-md, --text-ds-body-default, etc.

cssArchitecture.criticalWarning: theme.css has FIVE top-level blocks: :root { ... } → @media (max-width: 767px) { :root { ... } } → .spacing-compact { ... } → .dark { ... } → @theme inline { ... }. A previous error nested blocks inside :root by missing a closing brace, which broke all Tailwind utility classes. Always verify this structure is maintained. The @media block for responsive overrides MUST come before .spacing-compact so that compact mode always takes precedence.

fileOrganization./src/app/components/ds/: All 35 design system components + index.ts barrel export.
fileOrganization./src/app/components/ui/: shadcn primitives (Tooltip, Sheet) — never imported directly by pages, only by DS wrappers.
fileOrganization./src/app/pages/home/: HomePage.tsx + section components (Hero, ProjectsSection, About, Contact).
fileOrganization./src/app/pages/case-study/: CaseStudyPage.tsx (router) + individual case studies (CaseStudyInvest.tsx, CaseStudyAudio.tsx, CaseStudyShipping.tsx).
fileOrganization./src/app/components/user-flow-diagram.ts: Page-level UserFlowDiagram component for visualizing user flows in case studies. NOT a DS primitive — lives outside /ds/. See pageSpecificComponents section.
fileOrganization./src/app/components/prototypes/: Interactive prototype screen components rendered as ReactNode frames inside IPhoneMockup. Organized by case study slug (e.g. /prototypes/invest/).
fileOrganization./src/imports/: Figma-exported SVG paths and raster image assets.

pageSpecificComponents.description: Components that are NOT part of the DS barrel export but are used in specific pages. They live outside /components/ds/ and follow DS token rules but are not universal primitives.

UserFlowDiagram.purpose: Two-layer horizontal flow visualization for case study design process sections. Shows phases with step cards, directional arrows, and always-visible tooltip annotations.

structure.layer1_flow: Horizontal flex of FlowPhase groups. Each phase has a label + step cards connected by ArrowSpacer directional arrows.
structure.layer2_tooltips: Always-visible annotation cards aligned beneath their corresponding step cards. Same flex proportions as Layer 1 for column alignment.

props.FlowStep: { line1: string; line2?: string; tooltip?: { title: string; description: string; position?: TooltipPosition } }

UserFlowDiagram.styling: Uses DS tokens exclusively. Step cards: bg-ds-surface-page, border-ds-border-subtle, rounded-ds-sm. Tooltips: bg-ds-surface-inverse, text-ds-text-inverse, rounded-ds-sm. Phase labels: ds-text-label-sm, text-ds-text-tertiary.
UserFlowDiagram.responsiveness: Scrolls horizontally on viewports < MacBook Pro 16 inch. TooltipPointer uses only CSS longhand properties.
usedIn: CaseStudyInvest.tsx — Design Process section (variant B, replaces ProcessGrid)

PrototypeScreens.purpose: Interactive React components that render inside IPhoneMockup as ReactNode frames. Each screen simulates a real app screen with scrollable content, interactive elements, and DS-styled UI.
PrototypeScreens.usage: Passed as elements in the mockupFrames array of ProjectCard (imageVariant='mockup'): mockupFrames={[<AssetInfoScreen />]}. The scrollHint prop on ProjectCard signals users to scroll these interactive frames.
PrototypeScreens.addingNew: Create a new directory under /prototypes/ named after the case study slug. Export screen components from an index.tsx barrel. Each screen should use DS tokens and be sized for the 390×804 IPhoneMockup viewport.

do: Use DS components from /components/ds/ for all UI. Import from the barrel: import { X, Y } from '../../components/ds'
Use composite text classes (ds-text-body-default, ds-text-heading-hero, etc.) instead of individual font Tailwind utilities.
Use DS spacing utilities (px-ds-24, gap-ds-48) instead of arbitrary values.
Use DS color utilities (text-ds-text-primary, bg-ds-surface-background) for all colors.
Use DS radius utilities (rounded-ds-sm, rounded-ds-lg) for all border radius.
Wrap content blocks in MotionReveal for scroll-reveal animations.
Use TechnicalSheet as the universal text block — it handles subtitle + title + description + children + badges + CTA.
Use CaseStudySection for all case study page sections.
Alternate accent={true/false} on case study sections for visual rhythm.
Use unsplash_tool for all images — never hallucinate image URLs.
Give every list item a unique key prop based on data content.
Keep Inter as the only typeface. Hierarchy comes from size and tracking, not weight variety.
Rely on Layer 1 responsive token overrides for typography/spacing scaling — they work automatically via CSS variables. Don't add manual font-size breakpoints in components.
Use flex-col md:flex-row (or lg:) for layouts that need to stack on mobile. Pair with responsive gap utilities (gap-ds-24 md:gap-ds-48).
When adding new responsive token overrides, add them to the @media (max-width: 767px) block in theme.css, placed BEFORE .spacing-compact.
Use max-w-(--ds-max-w-content) for all homepage section content wrappers — the token is defined in theme.css and resizes every section at once.
Give every project in ProjectData a dedicated alt string separate from its title.
Store all per-project values (zoom, alt, showCta, slug) in the ProjectData array — keep JSX render logic data-agnostic.
dont: Never hardcode hex colors, pixel spacing, or font sizes. Always use CSS variables or DS utility classes.
Never import from /components/ui/ in pages — always use the DS wrapper (DSTooltip, MobileNav).
Never use raw motion.div for scroll-reveal — use MotionReveal instead.
Never use parallax effects outside of ParallaxHero on case study pages.
Never nest @theme inline inside :root in theme.css — it must be a top-level directive.
Never add font imports outside of /src/styles/fonts.css.
Never modify protected files: ImageWithFallback.tsx, pnpm-lock.yaml.
Never recreate patterns that already exist as DS components (e.g., don't manually build subtitle+title+description — use TechnicalSheet).
Never use location.state inside case study components (stale due to FrozenOutlet). Use URL search params instead.

Prefer weights 400 (Regular) and 500 (Medium) for all DS components. Weights 600 (SemiBold) and 700 (Bold) are loaded and reserved for the Navigation brand button only — do not use them elsewhere without explicit design direction.
Never add per-component font-size media queries — typography scaling is handled globally by Layer 1 token overrides in theme.css.
Never place the @media responsive block AFTER .spacing-compact in theme.css — compact mode must always win via source order.
Never use max-w-7xl or hardcoded max-w-[1386px] for homepage content columns — use max-w-(--ds-max-w-content) so the token controls every section.
Never put px-* on DesignSection via className — horizontal padding belongs on the Layer 2 content-wrapper div (see layout.sectionPadding).
Never wrap a grid of individually-revealed cards in an outer MotionReveal — the outer fade fires first, then each card tries to re-animate, causing a double-flash.
Never use raw Tailwind spatial utilities (e.g. bottom-12) — use the DS equivalent (bottom-ds-48) so spacing stays on the token scale.
Never compute alt text or zoom inline in JSX render — these belong in ProjectData alongside image, title, and slug.
